experiment_most_likely_to_show_strategy_.design: First reuse the existing cursor factorial. Then, only as a new experiment, compare baseline versus frozen guarded behavior crossed with default versus explicit fast-visible cursor motion on current exact lineage. Use eligible two-step and deliberately ineligible/ambiguous holdouts; no new admission rule. Include realistic provider latency and a near-zero provider control. experiment_most_likely_to_show_strategy_.why_this_is_adversarial: Legacy traces put roughly 76% of mock verified-outcome time in action waits, under 1% in semantic observations, and show about 2.9 s removable cosmetic work. A provider deletion saves work but cannot by itself erase those waits. The current guard is fixture-specific, so acceptance frequency must be visible rather than averaged away.

Guard overhead/fallback or low eligibility erases the provider savings on holdouts.
A claimed savings exists only in runner lifetime, not independently verified outcome time.
Any fresh-authority, mutation-journal or success regression appears: stop that arm immediately.
